out: Charity Prison Link Cymru warns that a chronic shortage of suitable housing is forcing many ex-offenders to live on the streets following their release. Experts argue that investing in affordable housing would be more cost-effective than the high price of re-incarcurating repeat offenders. While the Welsh Government reports increased support, advocates suggest that increasing the availability of one-bedroom properties is essential to prevent the cycle of homelessness and crime.

Police searched properties in the Waterfront Park and Colonsay View areas on Wednesday, resulting in the recovery of three firearms, ammunition, and a significant sum of money. A 26-year-old man was arrested and appeared in Edinburgh Sheriff Court on Thursday.

Four individuals appeared in a Chicago court facing multiple charges, including hate crimes and aggravated kidnapping, following the brutalization of an 18-year-old victim. Prosecutors allege the suspects kidnapped the victim and subjected him to horrific physical abuse while making derogatory statements in a viral Facebook Live video. Due to the severity of the crimes, the judge denied bail for all four suspects.

The former Arsenal goalkeeper and long-serving director of football has left his role at West Bromwich Albion. During his tenure, he played a key role in helping the club achieve promotion to the Premier League twice.

A new study involving mice shows that a "fasting-mimicking diet" can reverse diabetes symptoms by regenerating insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas. By cycling between periods of extreme calorie restriction and normal eating, the diet triggers a cellular "reprogramming" that restores organ function. Experts believe these findings could lead to significant new treatments for both type 1 and type 2 diabetes.

The proposed merger between Essilor and Luxottica would create a massive global eyewear behemoth, combining the world's leading lens and frame manufacturers. While the companies claim the deal will drive innovation and customer benefits, industry experts warn it could create a monopoly that reduces consumer choice and squeezes out competitors.

Olympic silver medallist Nicole Houvenaghel has accused British Cycling of "ageism" and a "win-at-all-costs" culture following a leaked report into the organization's failures. The report suggests that the pursuit of medals came at the expense of athlete welfare, leading to claims that investigations into misconduct were previously "sanised." British Cycling has since admitted to these governance failings and implemented a 39-point action plan to address cultural shortcomings.

After the 2009 recession, Kareem Badr successfully turned a failing Austin comedy club into a growing business by applying his computer science background to operational efficiency. 

As the popularity of stand-up comedy grows among younger audiences, clubs are increasingly finding success by combining entertainment with food and beverage services.

BT shares rose after regulators decided not to break up the giant telecoms company due to practical obstacles regarding its massive pension scheme. While the breakup was avoided, BT plans to introduce new articles of association to separate the management of its Openreach network, a move that could lead to future legal battles.

Ahead of the upcoming Old Firm derby, manager Brendan Rodgers expressed excitement about playing at Hampden Park, noting that the pitch will suit his team's high-intensity style.

Looking to build on a recent league victory, Rodgers emphasized that the team is focused on maintaining a high performance level to secure their first trophy of the season. While acknowledging the difficulty of achieving a domestic treble, he stated that winning the League Cup is a primary priority for the squad.

In response to an £8m subsidy cut, Queen's University plans to reduce its undergraduate student intake by 1,010 places over the next three years. This decision will lead to job losses among academic and non-academic staff, though the university stated there will be no compulsory redundancies.

University leaders and government ministers warned that these funding cuts could damage the institution's reputation and negatively impact the local economy by driving students and skilled workers to other parts of the UK.

An administrative error by an external printing company caused approximately 850 patients to receive incorrect leaflets suggesting their symptoms might indicate cancer. The East Sussex NHS Trust has apologized for the mistake, which occurred during a batch of appointment letters sent in March, and has contacted all affected individuals to explain the error.

Emily Thornberry has asserted that Labour will not "frustrate Brexit" even if the party's efforts to amend the draft legislation fail. Despite internal divisions and potential resignations over recent voting rebellions, the party aims to secure a "meaningful vote" on the final Brexit deal while respecting the public's decision to leave the EU.

The Republic of Ireland midfielder moved to AFC Bournemouth for an undisclosed fee, which includes a 15% sell-on clause benefiting his former club. Manager Paul Nicholson stated that the transfer funds will be used to support the cash-strapped club rather being distributed to individuals. The club is currently seeking new owners following significant budget cuts and the closure of its academy.

An inquest is ongoing following the death of 36-year-old Iwan Wyn Lewis, whose body was found in the Menai Strait after he was sectioned for allegedly assaulting his mother. A consultant psychiatrist testified that a police visit regarding bail arrangements may have contributed to Mr Lewis's distress and agitation prior to his death.

After signing a one-year deal this summer, 33-year-old former Blackpool forward Taylor-Fletcher has made only two appearances for the 13th-placed Owls this season. He joined the club following a campaign where he scored three goals in 23 games.

As the Trump administration prepares to take power, many US scientists are rushing to mirror and copy research data to own servers to prevent future censorship. This move comes following concerns that the incoming administration may curb access to climate research or target scientists who support mainstream views on global warming. Experts warn that restricting access to taxpayer-funded data would be a disservice to the public and could hinder global scientific progress.

The legendary drummer John "Brad" Bradbury, a founding member of the ska-reggae band The Specials, has passed away in England. His family and peers expressed deep regret over the loss of the musician, whose powerful drumming was a key element of the band's iconic sound. This news comes just three months after the death of the band's trombonist, Rico Rodriguez.

Tiger Woods missed the cut at Torrey Pines after shooting a second-round 72, marking his first full PGA Tour event in 18 months following a back injury. Along with other top players like Jason Day, Dustin Johnson, and Jimmy Walker, Woods failed to qualify for the next round as Rose took the lead.

Former Manchester United forward Alan Cole is currently recovering from a serious kidney failure that has prevented him from playing in a recent legends match. Despite the difficult recovery process, Cole has regained much of his physical fitness and hopes to be ready for future matches. Additionally, Cole expressed skepticism regarding English clubs' ability to compete with top European teams, noting the significant gap in player quality.

Pakistan has lifted its ban on YouTube after Google launched a localized version of the service that allows for more efficient content filtering. While the government and YouTube maintain that the process will follow specific guidelines, activists are calling for greater transparency regarding the terms of the agreement.

Following a recent injury sustained during a match against Exeter, 26-year-old player Benjamin is expected to be sidelined for the remainder of the season. Despite a history of injury struggles, Director of rugby Richard Cockerill confirmed that the injury is not serious and a full recovery is expected within eight to ten weeks. Meanwhile, the club also announced that scrum-half Sam Harrison has signed a new contract.

The Welshman rider Doull helped Great Britain win an Olympic gold medal in the team pursuit, setting a new world record. This victory marks a significant moment of redemption for Doull and contributes to Wales' successful Olympic run.

As floodwaters recede in several Indian states, the death toll has doubled with over 100 bodies discovered, and officials estimate that 450,000 people have been affected. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to visit Assam this Tuesday to address the recurring flooding crisis and discuss permanent solutions. Meanwhile, some residents in Gujarat have begun returning to their villages as aid packages are announced.

Two snowsports enthusiasts, Bridget and Jonathan Reid, recently married at the Nevis Range ski resort in Scotland, sliding down a run in their wedding attire. The couple chose the mountain setting to honor their shared love for skiing, which has been a central part of their relationship for six years.

Hong Kong regulators fined RBS following the conviction of former trader Shirlina Tsang for fraud involving falsified emerging markets trade records. While the regulator noted "significant weaknesses" in the bank's internal controls, the fine was mitigated due to RBS's prompt cooperation with authorities once the illegal activity was discovered.

Backstage at the BAFTA awards, winners Emma Stone, Tom Holland, and Viola Davis shared reflections on their recent successes and the importance of industry veterans like Meryl Streep. 

The ceremony also featured heartfelt moments from winners like Casey Affleck and Dev Patel, who discussed the impact of their roles and the significance of their achievements.

Despite a recent loss to world number 90 Jordan Thompson, concerns regarding Andy Murray's hip injury and physical fatigue are growing as he prepares for Wimbledon. While his Grand Slam record remains formidable, his recent struggles with injury and inconsistent movement have raised questions about his ability to maintain his dominance on grass. His upcoming performance at the French Open will serve as a key indicator of his readiness for the tournament at the All England Club.

Mandla Hlatshwayo, a well-known radio DJ, and his friend were shot after they attempted to stop a group of men robbing women at a Soweto pub. 

The suspects were apprehended with drugs and an unlicensed firearm, and police are currently questioning them to determine their involvement in the shooting. 

Tributes are pouring in for the 40-year-old star, who was remembered by those who knew him as a selfless man.

Police are investigating after shots were fired near two primary schools in Liverpool, which fortunately resulted in no injuries. While students were ordered to stay indoors as a precaution, the headteacher confirmed that pupils remained safe and the school day continued as planned. Authorities believe the attack was a targeted incident involving a vehicle and are currently reviewing CCTV and conducting inquiries.

Olympic champion Jessica Ennis-Hill currently holds third place at the Gotzis Hypo-Meeting after a strong first day of heptathlon competition. While she is still on track to qualify for the Rio Olympics, she must maintain her performance in the final 800m event to secure her spot.

The Formula 1 team Manor has officially ceased trading after failing to find a buyer during an administration process. The collapse resulting in staff redundancies leaves the grid reduced to 20 cars ahead of the upcoming season in Australia. Following the news, calls have been made for a European Commission investigation into the FIA and Formula One Group regarding the financial structures that led to the team's failure.

The upcoming Stormont election on 2 March will feature 228 candidates vying for 90 available seats, with the DUP and Sinn Féin fielding the largest numbers of candidates. The race includes a diverse field of political parties and 22 independent candidates, with candidate numbers varying from nine to 15 per constituency.

In response to a traveler's inquiry regarding currency exchange, expert Anthony Reuben suggests that the exchange rate fluctuates based on economic strength and political stability. He recommends "hedging bets" by purchasing currency in two installments to mitigate risk and advises using online comparison sites to avoid high airport fees.

Nineteen-year-old student Zoe Waters was declared the winner of the Alternative Model of the Year competition in Newcastle this Saturday. Waters, who expressed her desire to prioritize personal style over mainstream fashion, now plans to pursue a professional modeling career. The event was designed to celebrate diverse sub-cultures and provide a platform for individuals who do not fit traditional beauty standards.

The National Museum of the Royal Navy is proposing to move the Falklands War "Yomper" statue from Eastney to the Portsmouth Historic Dockyard as part of a museum relocation.

Local campaigners and the Portsmouth City Council are fighting the move, arguing that the memorial belongs at its current seaside location to be properly appreciated. While the museum director notes the move would increase visitor numbers, no final decision has been made as public consultations continue.

A suspect appeared at the Old Bailey facing charges for allegedly failing to contact a monitoring company and failing to report to a police station. This is believed to be the first case involving a breach of the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures (TPim). The defendant has been granted unconditional bail while remaining subject to his existing restrictions.

Former Sussex cricketer Anyon Seamer has been appointed as the new head coach of the women's senior side, as he also will lead the under-19 and under-21 teams. He succeeds Charlotte Burton and will work alongside Alexia Walker, who moves into a role supporting the senior, under-21, and under-19 squads.
Following a trial with the Shakers, 23-year-old defender Wes Brown has joined Bury. The experienced Football League player is available for the club's upcoming season opener against Doncaster.

Directed by Kenneth Branagh, the live-action adaptation of *Cinderella* has earned $70m at its opening weekend due to its decision to remain faithful to the original fairy tale. While the film eschets modern updates, the cast and director suggest that its classic storytelling allows audiences to find their own contemporary connections within the story.

For the first time in Eurovision history, the host nation, Ukraine, barred Russia from participating after the Russian singer was accused of violating Ukrainian border laws. This decision follows a political dispute regarding the singer's previous visit to Crimea, leading to a standoff between the two nations. While Eurovision organizers expressed disappointment over the move, Russia declined an offer to participate via satellite, further heightening the political tension surrounding the contest.

Reflecting on his experiences as a regular at the Cavern, Alex McKechnie recalls how the Beatles stood out to the local audience through their charismatic, irreverent performances. He notes that while they played standard covers, the band's ability to play complex chords and their rebellious, "punk-like" attitude made them the epitome of rebellion in Liverpool.

The South African government moves toward the introduction of a national minimum wage to combat poverty and inequality, though critics warn it may lead to higher unemployment. While the ruling party supports the proposal, opposition parties argue the amount is too low to sustain a household, with some calling for much higher rates. The decision comes amid sensitive political tensions and economic concerns regarding the country's credit rating and labor stability.

The death of Ethiopian leader Meles Zenawi, a complex and charismatic figure, has sparked fears of a power struggle in Addis Ababa that could destabilize the entire Horn of Africa. While his legacy is contested, he was a formidable regional strategist who oversaw significant economic modernization and the overthrow of a former dictatorship. His reign was marked by a tension between progressive ideals of social justice and an increasingly autocratic political environment that left many citizens in poverty.

Due to weather conditions at the MCG, play was abandoned after only 50.5 overs were possible, leaving Australia with a significant advantage. Despite the shortened match, Australia's bowlers took regular wickets, including a half-century from Azhar that helped secure their lead in the series.

In the recent Leith Walk by-election, the SNP and Scottish Labour successfully secured two seats using the Single Transferable Vote (STV) system. John Lewis Ritchie of the SNP topped the vote, while Marion Donaldson of Scottish Labour secured the second seat.

Tensions between the US and Russia have escalated over the collapse of a recent Syrian ceasefire, with the US warning that military talks may be suspended if Moscow halts its bombing. 

While Russia maintains it will continue supporting the Syrian government and urges the US to better distinguish between rebels and terrorists, the US maintains that the current lack of cooperation makes continued negotiations difficult. Amidst these diplomatic struggles, the humanitarian crisis in Aleppo has intensified, leaving thousands of civilians trapped in appalling conditions.

Both players, Hooker Hughes and flanker Evans, have been selected for the Welsh squad for the upcoming Junior World Championship in June. Following a successful Six Nations campaign, the pair will look to build momentum as they compete in Pool A against Ireland, Georgia, and New Zealand.

The outgoing Obama administration has announced new sanctions against Russia in response to allegations of election interference and cyber-activity, characterizing these actions as a necessary defense against Russian efforts to destabilize democracy.

In response, Russian officials have condemned the move as a vindistic attempt to sabotage U-Russian relations and sabotage the incoming Trump administration. They argue the accusations are baseless attempts to cover up the failures of American foreign policy.

Jeremy Corbyn is proposing a complete reversal in policy by abolishing university tuition fees to ensure that cost and debt no longer deter potential students. This move represents a shift from market-driven funding to direct government support, aiming to appeal to younger voters and treat free education as a fundamental principle. While the plan aims to eliminate the growing burden of student debt, some universities warn that moving away from fee-based funding could limit student numbers and prevent the expansion of higher education.

Emergency crews have finished their recovery operations at the A27 crash site following the fatal jet crash that killed eleven people. While the physical work at the scene is complete, police and investigators continue to work closely with victims' families and seek to interview the pilot. The single closed westbound lane is expected to reopen to traffic next week.

During Senate testimony, intelligence chiefs Dan Coats and Admiral Mike Rogers refused to discuss private conversations with President Trump regarding the Russia investigation, citing the need to protect sensitive information. The officials' reluctance to provide details frustrated senators and followed reports that the president attempted to influence the probe into Michael Flynn.

A private party hosted by the Obamas was attended by approximately 500 guests, including high-profile CEOs, lobbyists, and celebrities like Tyler Perry and Angela Bassett. The event featured performances by Prince and Stevie Wonder, which Al Sharpton described as "awesome."

In the BBC series *Doctor in the House*, Dr. Rangan helped 34-year-old Emma Gleeson manage her severe anxiety and panic attacks through significant dietary changes. By replacing processed foods with fresh ingredients and reducing sugar, Emma experienced improved mood, increased energy, and a reduction in her daily panic attacks.

The Alabama Securities Commission has closed an investigation into whether Harper Lee was manipulated to publish her new book, *Go Set a Watchman*. Investigators concluded that Lee was able to answer questions to their satisfaction, suggesting she consented to the release of the manuscript. While the move sparked concerns regarding the elderly author's capacity, her lawyer maintains that Lee was "extremely hurt" by the allegations of manipulation.

The United States has suspended bilateral talks with Russia over the failure to maintain a ceasefire and the continued Russian-backed attacks on civilians in Aleppo. While Washington accuses Moscow of failing to prevent Syrian regime strikes on critical infrastructure, Russia claims the U.S is merely shifting blame for the collapsed truce. Although diplomatic channels are being halted, both nations intend to maintain communication regarding counter-terrorism operations to avoid direct military clashes.

Sadiq Khan's victory as London's first Muslim mayor has drawn significant international attention, with global leaders and media outlets reflecting on the historical and political implications of his win. Many commentators view his election as a landmark moment for social mobility and a symbolic victory over rising Islamophobia in Europe.

After a traditional advertisement failed to attract applicants, parishioners at St Paul's in Shipley posted a viral video featuring children singing about their requirements for a new vicar. The video, which lists qualities like a cheery disposition and a love for Harry Potter, has been viewed over 3000 times and gained widespread media coverage. The new vicar, Henriette Howarth, is set to begin her post next week.

Belgium international Kevin De Bruyne is expected to be out for approximately 10 weeks following an injury sustained during a recent match. The absence will force him to miss several key fixtures, including the League Cup final and crucial Champions League matches.

A 27-year-old Swiss man died following a stabbing and arson attack on a train that left five other passengers injured, including a six-year-old child. 

Police investigation into the incident suggests the attacker acted alone and that there is currently no indication of a political or terrorist motive.

A Flybe passenger aircraft narrowly avoided a collision after a drone was flown within the air traffic zone near Cornwall Airport Newquay. Police and aviation authorities are investigating the incident, which they described as a reckless disregard for public safety. Authorities are currently appealing to the public for information to help identify the drone operator.

A large grey seal was rescued at Cruden Bay after becoming tangled in unprecedented amounts of fishing netting around its neck. The Scottish SPCA successfully removed the netting at their rescue centre, and later released the healthy seal back into the water.

The National Library of Scotland has completed a year-long project to catalogue the archive of the late travel writer and war hero, Sir Patrick Leigh Fermor. The collection includes rare manuscripts, personal letters from notable historical figures, and a unique notebook from his 1913 trek across Europe. The library now plans to digitize the collection and host exhibitions to share these pieces of 20th-century history with the public.

Mr. Roache has been elected as the new general secretary of the GMB union, winning 56.7% of the vote to succeed Paul Kenny. With 35 years of experience at the union, Mr. Roache aims to lead a "21st-century union" that fights for its 600,000 members and their communities.

Despite her self-described "terror" regarding stage fright, singer Annie Mac is preparing for a major career milestone with the release of her new album, *The Dreaming Room*. The artist is set to perform on the prestigious music show *Later... with Jools Holland*, a moment she views as both a terrifying challenge and a significant professional honor.

After battling a cancer diagnosis and undergoing chemotherapy, Newcastle player Jonas Gutierrez expressed his emotional relief at returning to professional football. He stated that he feels "born again" and is now focused on working hard to prove he can still compete at the Premier League level.

Exeter City reported a £1.42m profit for the 2014-15 period, primarily driven by the record-breaking sale of midfielder Matt Grimes. Despite facing emergency loan requirements and transfer embargoes due to cashflow issues, the club successfully reduced its cost base and increased its shareholder funds. The board now plans to reinvest the transfer income into improving the club's infrastructure and redeveloping St James Park.

Emirati para-athlete Abdullah Hayayei has tragically passed away while training at a London leisure centre ahead of the World Para-athletics Championships. The incident occurred when a training cage collapsed on him, and police are currently investigating the circumstances of the accident. A moment of silence will be held in his honor during the championships' opening ceremony this Friday.

Despite economic data showing weakness in the Scottish economy, a survey by the Scottish Chambers of Commerce reveals a more optimistic growth across several sectors, particularly in manufacturing and retail.

While business optimism remains generally positive, firms are facing challenges such as rising prices, skill shortages, and fluctuating sales revenues.

The outlook for 2017 remains balanced, as success will depend on businesses' ability to manage rising costs and maintain consumer demand amidst economic pressures.

An inquiry in London has launched to investigate allegations of human rights abuses and potential miscarriages of justice involving undercover policing. The proceedings aim to examine whether officers used deceptive tactics, such as entering long-term romantic relationships, to gather intelligence on activist groups. The final report will provide recommendations to the Home Office regarding the future deployment and management of undercover officers.

In a brutal, physical encounter, the All Blacks secured a two-point victory over South Africa to advance to the next round of the World Cup. Despite being a man down at halftime, New Zealand overcame early penalties to turn the game around through a Dan Carter drop-goal and a Beauden Barrett try. The champions ultimately withstood a ferocious Springbok defense to maintain their lead and remain favorites to retain the trophy.

The National Trust uses ground-penetrating radar and wind sensors to conduct a crucial survey of the historic Wellington monument in Somerset. This study aims to identify structural voids and material composition to create a computer model for more effective future repairs.

The world's largest clothing retailer, Inditex, reported an 8% increase in net earnings to €26bn, driven by an 11% jump in sales. This growth was fueled by the expansion of its online presence into new territories and significant investments in mobile payment technology.

The company's strong performance, bolstered by steady economic growth in Spain, sets it apart from competitors like H&M and Next.

Lady Gaga is preparing for a spectacular Super Bowl performance in Houston, aiming to even out-do the legendary shows of past performers. The article reflects on iconic moments in Super Bowl history, ranging from Michael Jackson’s dramatic entrance to Beyoncé’s political set and Diana Ross's high-energy performance.

Following the release of the documentary *The Betrayed Girls*, victims of the 2012 Rochdale grooming scandal have warned that similar patterns of exploitation remain ongoing in Greater Manchester. 

While authorities and local councils claim they have learned vital lessons and are committed to tackling abuse, former prosecutor Nazir Afzal warned that many victims still feel their reports are being ignored or dismissed.

A heavy water leak caused a ceiling collapse and significant stock damage at the Victoria Centre store on Tuesday. The store is now closed until further notice as staff and management work around the clock to clean up and repair the damage.

Experts have detected a massive influx of over 400,000 automated, bot-driven comments to the FCC regarding net neutrality proposals. The activity, which features identical wording and data pulled from breached databases, is being viewed as a new form of digital protest. However, critics warn that these artificial submissions could muddy the waters by masking genuine public opinion and providing the FCC with an excuse to dismiss real opposition.

Following a period of declining attendance since their 2012 stadium move, Sale Sharks' new board is launching a rebuilding effort to improve the matchday experience and club culture. The new leadership aims to transform the stadium infrastructure and restore the club as a competitive force in the North of England.

Disney's *Moana* earned $81.1m in its debut, marking the second-highest Thanksgiving opening of all time, despite controversy regarding its promotional merchandise. Other films like *Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them* and Brad Pitt's *Allied* also saw varying levels of success at the box office.

The third seed, world number 18 Emma Konta, secured a dominant 6-3, 6-1 victory over an American wildcard in just one hour. Her performance included 11 aces as she advanced to the quarter-finals. She will next face China's Saisai Zheng on Friday.

Two men were taken to the hospital with injuries following an attack on Linn Road this Sunday afternoon. Police are currently appealing for anyone with information regarding the incident to contact them.

Researchers investigating the source of Emile’s fatal Ebola infection discovered that the boy likely contracted the virus through contact with bat droppings while playing in a hollowed tree in his village.

The study suggests that the outbreak was a rare occurrence caused by specific environmental conditions rather than the consumption of bushmeat.

The findings emphasize the importance of understanding bat-to-human transmission and highlight that protecting these insect-eating animals is vital to preventing other diseases like malaria.

World number two and snooker player Bing Bingham is uncertain about his participation in this year's tournament due to his wife's impending labor. He will decide whether to play his first-round match against Joe Perry after consulting with his wife regarding the timing of the birth.

The council has voted to begin urgent dismantling of parts of the Grade II pier to prevent further collapse and ensure safety. Because the structure is deemed dangerous, officials decided to bypass the usual consent process to begin work immediately. While some parts of the pier will be saved and stored, the total cost of the project remains uncertain despite a £650,000 budget allocation.

The Campaign to Protect Rural England (CPRE) is seeking a judicial review to stop the £21.5m Castle Mill development at Oxford, over concerns regarding its impact on the historic skyline and local environment. While the council maintains the project is complete and the claims are unfounded, the university intends to occupy the buildings by October to meet academic deadlines.

The Olympus Trust, which operates several schools near Bristol, has warned that government funding cuts are leading to a "crisis point" that may force decisions such as shortening school days or cutting staff.

While the Department for Education claims new funding plans will increase the trust'wide budget, parents and unions have condemned the potential cuts as "diabolical" and harmful to student support.

Efforts by developing nations to expand forest reserves to curb carbon emissions may lead to the displacement of millions of local residents, particularly in Liberia and the DR Congo. Experts warn that these conservation efforts often ignore the rights of indigenous communities who have historically acted as the most effective protectors of the land. To prevent violent conflict and human rights abuses, advocates argue that international funding should support local livelihoods rather than forcing people off their ancestral territories.

A human skull and additional skeletal remains were discovered by workers near the M54 slip road in Telford. West Mercia Police are investigating the discovery, noting that the remains likely belonged to an adult male and had been there for at least two years. The investigation is in its early stages, and authorities are coordinating with neighboring forces to identify missing persons.

In the Olympic boxing competition, 23-year-old Dusmatov secured a unanimous points victory to advance through the tournament. Meanwhile, Martinez became the first Colombian Olympic boxing finalist, while Americans Nico Hernandez and Joahnys Argilagos secured bronze after losing their respective semi-final matches.

University support staff are currently balloting on a 1.1% pay offer, with unions describing the increase as an "insult" while potential strike action is looming for the autumn.

The unions argue that staff have suffered significant real-terms pay cuts, whereas employers maintain the offer is the best available and represents a limit of affordability.

The Scottish government has "called in" a proposal to merge and close St Joseph's Primary in Milngavie, following protests from local parents and the Catholic Church. The decision comes due to concerns that the council's consultation process may have contained inaccurate information or failed to address issues raised by Education Scotland.

Kazuyoshi Miura, the legendary Japanese striker known as "King Kazu," has signed to continue playing for his second-division club past his 49th birthday. His decision extends a historic career that has spanned over 30 years and includes significant achievements with the Japanese national team.

Violence in the Kashmir region has escalated following the anniversary of the death of militant leader Burhan Wani, leading to deadly clashes between protesters and security forces. Meanwhile, shelling across the Line of Control has resulted in at least seven deaths, with both India and Pakistan trading blame for the casualties. The unrest comes amid heavy security restrictions and ongoing conflict over the disputed territory.

A Leave vote was widely viewed as a potential source of significant financial instability, particularly regarding bank liquidity and sharp exchange rate fluctuations. To mitigate these risks, central banks have prepared various strategies, such as providing liquidity to banks or intervening in currency markets using national reserves.

Veteran back-row forward Christian else is leaving Sale Sharks after several successful years, as he plans to transition into a teaching career. He will depart following the season' finale to begin a teaching position at Wrekin College in Shropshire.

An investigation into the closed Tawel Fan ward at Glan Clwyd Hospital has revealed that inadequate care may contributed to the deaths of several patients. The Betsi Cadwaladr health board is currently conducting a thorough investigation to determine the full extent of the failings and provide answers to grieving families.

While Khan was described by his former partner as a hardworking and accomplished professional, the group has been remanded in custody and awaits sentencing on April 15.

The British Transport Police will begin deploying Taser stun weapons to officers in Scotland to address a mounting international terrorism threat. This decision brings the Scottish force in parity with English counterparts and provides officers with an additional option to protect the public and themselves during high-risk incidents. Every use of the device will be subject to strict internal reviews and oversight from the Police Investigations and Review Commissioner.

ID Systems, an industrial utilities company, has secured funding and equity backing from UKSE to facilitate a major expansion drive. This investment will allow the company to more than double its workforce across the Glasgow and Lanarkshire areas following several significant contract wins.

Following the fatal plane crash that killed 71 people, investigators are looking into evidence suggesting the aircraft ran out of fuel despite prior warnings from the pilot. While several survivors, including Chapecoense defender Helio Hermito Zampier Neto, remain in stable condition after surgery, the aviation authority has suspended the operating license of the charter airline involved.

Anti-tunnel campaigners and historians joined a protest against Highways England's proposed dual carriageway tunnel at Stonehenge, arguing that the project would permanently damage the site's wider archaeological significance. While the scheme has backing from English Heritage and the National Trust, critics argue the current proposal is "old-fashioned" and fails to protect the landscape's true heritage. Highways England maintains that the project aims to reduce congestion and enhance the World Heritage Site by removing traffic from the immediate vicinity.

Everton secured a 4-0 victory over Wolfsburg to move to the top of Group H in the Europa League. A strong starting lineup led by manager Roberto Martinez delivered an attacking performance featuring goals from an own goal, a header, and a penalty.

Pawel Sroka, 33, has been charged with the murder of his partner, 29-year-old Joanna Trojniak. A post-mortem examination determined that Ms. Trojniak died from a stab wound to the chest. Sroka is scheduled to appear in Bromley Magistrates' Court on April 4.

Prostate cancer is often overlooked due to societal-driven reluctance toward medical consultation, leading to high mortality rates among men. To combat this, researchers are developing advanced radiotherapy techniques and have identified new genetic markers that could lead to more effective screening and targeted treatments. These breakthroughs aim to improve diagnostic accuracy and patient outcomes for a disease that has historically been under-priorized in oncology research.

Wasps secured a vital victory and a place in the end-of-season play-offs despite playing with 14 men after Bryce Heem was sent off. 

The match saw multiple red cards and high-scoring exchanges, ultimately resulting in a win for the hosts that keeps them competitive in the league standings.

Following a deadly terrorist attack in Tunisia claimed by ISIS, which resulted in many foreign casualties, the Tunisian Prime Minister has dismissed six police chiefs after admitting security shortcomings. In response to the tragedy, a massive march against terrorism is planned for Sunday, with President Francois Hollande expected to attend.

By leveling buildings and digging trenches into runways, the militants have rendered the airport useless for attackers while clearing lines of sight for their own defensive positions. This scorched-earth tactic mirrors previous demolitions used to delay enemy advances and complicate the repair of vital assets.

Major engineering work on the line between Reading and London Paddington is scheduled to take the form of significant disruption over the Easter break. Network Rail officials stated that they have organized hundreds of replacement buses to mitigate any potential delays, following previous project overruns last year. The work aims to resolve a major national bottleneck and complete the final stages of the Reading station redevelopment.

Plans have been approved for Coastal Oil and Gas Limited to conduct exploratory drilling at St Nicholas, though the permit specifically excludes any hydraulic fracturing. Natural Resources Wales stated that the project will be strictly monitored to protect the environment, with all work and land reinstatement completed within 12 months. This decision comes amid a temporary ban on fracking in Wales as the government awaits further devolution of decision-making powers.

Amazon is transitioning its tax structure from Luxembourg to local branches in the UK, Germany, Spain, and Italy to register sales within those specific countries. This move follows years of criticism and formal investigations by the European Union into tax avoidance policies and illegal state aid.

Junior doctors in England have begun industrial action over disputes regarding new contract terms and weekend pay, after negotiations with the government failed to reach a resolution. While the BMA maintains the strikes demonstrate professional unity, critics like Dame Sally Davies warn that the action could lead to patient suffering.

Nineteen-year-old player Kenny has become eligible to play in this Sunday's Football League Trophy final against Barnsley. Oxford head coach Michael Appleton praised the young talent, noting his bright future and his successful integration into the squad.

Kingston Maurward College and Weymouth College have been awarded significant grants to fund major building refurbishment and facility upgrades. These investments are part of a national initiative to ensure colleges possess first-rate facilities to support high-quality teaching and vocational skills.

The family of former footballer Jeff Astle has met with FA chairman Greg Dyke to discuss the risks of head injuries and concussion in football. Following a medical finding that Astle's death was linked to brain damage from heading heavy footballs, his family is campaigning for better player education and medical policies. The meeting aims to highlight the importance of addressing brain-related injuries to protect the lives of current and future players.

As the global wealth gap reaches its widest point in 30 years, experts discuss the increasing divide between the ultra-wealthy and the rest of society. While the number of billionaires is growing, the widening disparity is making social mobility harder and fueling public hostility toward the elite. Some experts suggest that while luck plays a role in wealth accumulation, there may need to be limits on inherited wealth to ensure greater opportunity for future generations.

Identical 18-year-old twins have made significant impressions at Sale Sharks after appearing in nine Premiership matches this season. The pair, who both represent England Under-20s, are seen as key components of the club's long-term player development vision.

Police are searching for a man following an incident that occurred near Corbett Place and Calais View on Thursday morning. He is described as being in his late teens or early 20s, approximately 5ft 9in tall, with dark, curly, short hair and wearing a dark top. Officers are urging anyone with information to come in in contact.

An Egypt-backed proposal to establish a regional forum during NPT negotiations was blocked by the US, UK, and Canada, preventing a potential move that could force Israel to clarify its nuclear status.

The failure to reach a consensus means the next review will not takely place until 2022. While the US accused Egypt and other Arab nations of being unrealistic, Egypt warned that the failed deal would have political consequences within the Arab world.

The UK government has introduced measures to speed up fracking applications in England, but Natural Resources Minister Carl Sargeant has clarified that the temporary ban on fracking remains in place for Wales.

While the UK government supports oil and gas development to prevent delays, Welsh ministers maintain a focus on renewable energy due to environmental and safety concerns.

The tension highlights the differing approaches between English and Welsh authorities regarding energy production and sustainable development.

Following his stunning victory over Wladimir Klitschko, British boxer Fury has struggled with mental health issues and the loss of his championship belts after being banned. The article suggests that his sudden loss of focus and withdrawal from scheduled matches are the result of reaching his professional peak and failing to cope with the psychological toll of success.

Wasps boss Dai Young expects several of his in-form players to be considered for the upcoming England training camp and autumn Test series. While Leicester's young talent Will Evans is viewed as a "project player" not yet ready for international rugby, players like Mike Williams are considered ready for immediate selection. The squad announcement comes as England looks to fill voids in their backroom following recent injuries.

The Old Low Light Heritage Centre in North Shields hosts "From Dark to Light," the first major exhibition in his hometown dedicated to the artist Victor Noble Rainbird. The collection features previously unseen works, including paintings of the North Sea and poignant wartime drawings from his service on the Western Front. Running from 1 July to 6 September, the exhibition aims to shed new light on the life and legacy of this remarkable artist.

Former Celtic manager Neil Lennon and Scotland assistant Mark McGhee have welcomed Scott Brown's decision to reverse his retirement, noting that his return will provide a vital boost to the national squad. Both managers believe Brown's leadership and quality will be key assets as Scotland prepares for their upcoming World Cup qualifier against England.

A buzzard was rescued in Bethesda after becoming stuck in a wire fence while chasing a wood pigeon. Inspector Mike Pugh freed the animal and released it back into the wild with minimal feather damage.

Thousands of workers from Crown Post Offices will begin a walkout starting Monday, December 19, which includes Christmas Eve. The union is protesting planned branch closures and pension changes, while the Post Office maintains that services will remain "business as usual" at most locations. Both parties have agreed to resume talks this Wednesday to address the ongoing dispute.

During the launch of the Ulster Unionists' manifesto, Mike Nesbitt sparked controversy by suggesting he would rather form a government with the SDLP than with Sinn Féin.

The remarks, which suggest a willingness to transfer votes to nationalist-leaning parties, have caused friction within his own party.

Nesbitt maintains that his comments were not a mistake, framing his stance as a call for partnership over domination to ensure a stable government after the election.

Irish police and customs officials seized over 60,000 vials containing anabolic steroids and human growth hormones during raids in Muff and Lidford. The investigation uncovered evidence of an illegal manufacturing operation, leading to the arrest of a man in his 30s. Further searches have also been carried out in Northern Ireland as part of the ongoing operation.

Irish Prime Minister Enda Kenny suggested that a potential referendum on Irish unity could occur if Brexit negotiations trigger a clear majority desire to join the Republic. While supporters like Gerry Adams welcomed the possibility as an opportunity for unification, unionist politicians dismissed the comments as "mischaneous" and unlikely to happen. Critics argued that the priority should remain on managing the economic impacts of Brexit rather than discussing border polls.

After a strong start to the season, Morecambe has moved to the top of the league following a 1-0 win against Yeovil. Manager Bentley praised the team's disciplined approach and highlighted veteran Kevin Ellison's professionalism as a model for young players.

Qatar rejected a list of 13 conditions imposed by Saudi Arabia and its allies, claiming the demands are an attempt to limit the nation's sovereignty rather than combat terrorism. While U-states officials urged the parties to lower rhetoric and seek a diplomatic resolution, the blockading nations maintained that the measures are necessary to stop extremism. Despite the economic and diplomatic pressure, Qatar has avoided collapse by utilizing alternative trade routes through Iran and Turkey.

Due to a six-month suspension that she claims was an abuse of party rules, Ms. Evans has confirmed she is unable to run in the upcoming UKIP leadership contest. Instead of seeking the role, she has endorsed councillor Lisa Duffy to succeed Nigel Farage.

Ms. Evans stated that the party must undergo internal reform to move away its "hard-right image" and become a more professional political entity. She expressed that while she is disappointed by the leadership's actions, she remains determined to support the party's growth and renewal.

Following a high-profile rape case in Delhi, an Uber driver has reportedly confessed to the crime after being identified by his victim. This incident, which led to a ban on several web-based taxi firms, highlights ongoing concerns regarding sexual violence and the effectiveness of recent legal reforms in India.

Despite a loss to Portugal, the Welsh national team's historic Euro 2016 campaign was celebrated as a triumph due to the deep bond between players and their unwavering supporters. The tournament marked a significant breakthrough for Wales, breaking a decades-long psychological barrier and establishing the team as a competitive force on the international stage. This successful run has fostered a unique sense of national pride and a renewed connection between the players and the "Red Wall" of fans.

The latest Scottish Index of Multiple Deprivation (SIMD) results show that certain areas in Renfrewshire and Glasgow remain among the most deprived in Scotland. While local leaders argue that new strategic approaches are beginning to improve local fortunes, political parties are debating whether the causes are rooted in government policy or systemic socio-economic issues. The findings have sparked political debate regarding the best methods for tackling deep-seated poverty and inequality across the country.

British pair Cassells and Scrimgeour secured the European title in the lightweight pairs after finishing first in their semi-final. Meanwhile, Irish Olympic silver medallist Paul O'Donovan also saw success by winning his lightweight single sculls semi-final.

The 22-year-old former Kilmarnock player has signed a one-year contract to join the Scottish Championship club. He joins teammates Craig Barr and Mark Stewart, both of whom joined the club last summer.

Liverpool secured a 2-1 victory over Swansea through goals from Leroy Fer, Roberto Firmino, and a late winning penalty from James Milner. Despite a spirited first-half performance, Swansea's second-half collapse leaves manager Guidolin's future increasingly uncertain as the club remains near the relegation zone.

The recent positive steroid test in Scottish rugby has raised serious concerns regarding the growing pressure on players to increase their size and weight. The author suggests that the culture of intense weight training and supplement use among young players may be creating a dangerous path toward illegal performance-enhancing drugs.

The new TRNSMT festival at Glasgow Green will kick with Radiohead on opening night, followed by headlining sets from Kasabian and Biffy Clyro over the weekend. Replacing the suspended T in the Park, the event will feature three stages and strict security measures, including armed police patrols and a zero-tolerance policy toward drugs and intoxication.

North Korea has officially confirmed the restart of the Yongbyon reactor, a facility previously shut down as part of a 2007 disarmament deal. The White House responded by calling for North Korea to fulfill its international obligations and refrain from provocative actions that aggravate regional tensions. While the move signals an effort to improve nuclear capabilities, experts remain uncertain regarding the actual scale of the North's nuclear progress.

Following the reopening of a murder inquiry into the 2019 disappearance of 27-year-old Andrew Bedford, police have arrested a 64-year-old man after discovering human bones on land in Ramsey. 

The discovery occurred during a forensic search of an area of interest, leading investigators to believe Mr Bedford was shot in September 1990. Detectives are now conducting DNA testing on the remains as they seek further information to resolve the case.

Millionaire Marwan Koukash is aiming to transform Salford City Reds into a major rugby league powerhouse through ambitious recruitment and significant financial investment. To achieve this, Koukash is courting legendary coach Brian Noble and lobbying to raise the Super League salary cap to attract top-tier talent. While his bold plans have sparked debate, they have successfully placed the struggling club back at the center of the sporting conversation.

Led by a four-wicket haul from Isobel Joyce, Ireland secured a dominant victory over Zimbabwe to maintain a perfect record in the qualifying tournament. This win moves Ireland closer to securing a spot in next year's World Twenty20, with their placement depending on upcoming matches against Scotland.

Colchester Hospital has been rated as "inadequate" following a CQC inspection that found the facility relied on unsuitable agency staff and demonstrated poor leadership. The inspection findings have sparked outrage from the family of Norman Betchley, who died in 2009 due to agency staffing errors, claiming the issues remain unaddressed. While the hospital's chief executive acknowledged the challenge of reducing agency dependency, the trust remains in special measures as it works toward an improvement plan.

British cyclist Mark Cavendish secured a third-place overall position after a strong performance in various track cycling events, including a second-place finish in the individual pursuit. Meanwhile, Becky James set a new Olympic record during the women's sprint qualifications to advance into the quarter-finals.

Finance Minister Máirtín Ó Muilleoir has announced a reallocation of funds that will provide an additional £200m to the health sector for the 2016/17 period. This funding, which follows requests for more resources to meet growing demand, is expected to focus on unscheduled care and addressing hospital bed-blocking issues. Other reallocations will also support schools, road maintenance, and further education.

The Winklevoss twins have filed a new lawsuit against Facebook, alleging that the company suppressed crucial evidence during their previous legal battles over the origins of the site. This fresh legal action follows the dismissal of their attempt to appeal a 22-year-old settlement regarding the ownership of Facebook. Facebook's counsel has dismissed the claims as baseless allegations that have already been rejected by the courts.
A teenage pedestrian was struck by a Ford Focus in Rotherham on Saturday. The driver was not injured, and police are now appealing for witnesses to come forward.

Harry Chapman Pincher, a former *Daily Express* defense correspondent, was renowned for securing scoops through his ability to cultivate high-level contacts via social settings like lunching and game shooting. 

After his retirement, he published books alleging that Britain's security services had been penetrated by spies at the highest levels.

After initially rejecting a move, striker Stewart has agreed to personal terms and passed his medical to join Birmingham City. He is expected to make his debut this Saturday against Leeds following his arrival as the club's second signing of the week.

A former private has accepted a conditional caution for misconduct in a public office following an arrest during Operation Elveden. As part of the agreement, she will make a £40 payment to an armed forces charity to resolve the case.

The Care Inspectorate has issued low ratings to two Glasgow care homes, Nithsdale House and Drumpellier Lodge, following recent inspections. Inspectors highlighted significant concerns regarding the quality of care, staffing, and management, noting that both facilities failed to address requirements from previous inspections. The Care Inspectorate has warned that further action will be taken if the services do not show immediate and significant improvement.

Police arrested four men in Enfield on Saturday after reports of a firearm being seen in a vehicle. The suspects were taken into custody following a stop of the car and are currently being held at a north London police station.

A major power outage caused by a substation failure left thousands of properties in Lancaster, Morecambe, and Carnforth without electricity. The outage resulted in significant disruption to schools, businesses, and local government, as well well as travel issues and technical problems at Lancaster University. Power was fully restored to all affected areas by late afternoon, though the cause of the outage remains unknown.

A judge has quashed a decision by the Secretary of State to block housing development plans for the Hatchfield Farm estate in Newmarket. The ruling found that the refusal was "plainly deficient" and failed to properly assess the impact of the proposals. As a result, the planning application must now be reconsidered.

Following a series of mechanical failures, groundings, and safety suspensions since the launch of a new chain ferry, the council has ordered an official review of the project.

The council has temporarily waived crossing fees until July 2 to allow for feedback and to address the "frustrating" start to the service.

Local business owners are now calling for compensation as they face significant financial losses due to the ferry's operational issues.

Tunisia international Sliti has signed a three-year contract with Lille following a successful loan spell. The 24-year-old has made 16 appearances for the club, scoring one goal, as they currently sit 11th in the league table.

The British astronaut has spent six weeks in space, including time to engaging with children through video calls. During the mission, she also took time to share her experiments and connect with students back on Earth.

Martyn Irvine has been named the BBC Northern Ireland Sports Personality of the Year following his historic achievements in track cycling. The 28-year-old became the first Irish cyclist in 117 years to win a world title, while also securing a silver medal and a World Cup gold this year.

An Italian C-27J military aircraft was safely escorted to Prestwick Airport after losing communication while flying from Iceland to Italy. RAF Typhoon jets were launched to intercept the plane as a precaution, and although emergency services were summoned to the scene, the aircraft landed without incident. Local police are now leading the investigation into the incident.

Five men were arrested on suspicion of terrorism-related offenses following the discovery of two suspect devices at a business in Birmingham's Lee Bank area. The arrests were intelligence-led, and magistrates have granted police an additional seven days to question the suspects as investigations continue across several properties.

The upcoming football tournament in France will expand to 24 teams, with the group stage followed by a knockout format leading to the final on July 10. While hosts France and defending champions Spain are top contenders, the tournament features a competitive field including favorites Germany and debutants like Slovakia.

Greatment's men's basketball team will face Greece in a warm-up game at the Copper Box as they prepare for the 2017 FIBA EuroBasket. Following a recent loss to the Greek side, the game serves as a vital preparation match to ensure the team is ready for their upcoming tournament schedule. The match will be broadcast on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website.

Despite playing with 13 men for seven minutes, Australia secured a victory over Wales through a heroic defensive effort and the clinical kicking of Bernard Foley. Wales suffered their 11th consecutive defeat to the Wallabies, failing to capitalize on their numerical advantage during a frustrating loss. The win advances Australia to a quarter-final matchup against Scotland, while Wales prepares to face South Africa.

As Scotland prepares to face Ireland, players expressed a desire to give departing coach Gregor Townsend a successful farewell. Despite facing a highly-ranked Irish side and an experienced forward pack, the Scottish squad aims to use the emotional incentive of the coaching transition to fuel their performance.

In a rare interview, retired General Petraeus, the architect of the Iraq War "surge," warned that defeating "industrial-strength" extremists like IS cannot be achieved through military force alone. He argued that the recent loss of Ramadi highlights the need to refine strategies and ensure that political solutions are integrated with military efforts.

To combat the rise of IS, Petraeus emphasized that the Iraqi government must provide political incentives to Sunni Arabs to secure their support for the new Iraq.

The City of Edinburgh Council has reported a cyber attack on its website service provider that resulted in the theft of users' email addresses. Officials have notified the relevant authorities and implemented extra security measures, warning that affected individuals may see an increase in spam or phishing attempts.

Following an increase in violence and attacks on residential areas, several rebel groups have formed a joint operations room to launch new offensives in Syria. In the wake of this escalating fighting, the Syrian opposition delegation has expressed its intent to suspend formal peace talks in Geneva over concerns regarding the deteriorating humanitarian situation. While the US has called on Russia to pressure the Syrian government to uphold the ceasefire, the future of the fragile peace process remains uncertain.

To own its future and build a sustainable business, Instagram plans to introduce advertisements within a few months to generate revenue from its 150 million users. Despite previously facing backlash over privacy concerns, the company aims to tap into the booming global social media advertising market to finally turn a profit.

The 2016 Hyundai Mercury Prize will take on September 15 at the Hammersmith Apollo, featuring a lineup of nominees such as Radiohead and the acts associated with David Bowie's *Blackstar*. The ceremony will feature a public vote to select a finalist, followed by a panel of judges choosing the overall winner.

Gurpal Virdi, a retired detective from the Metropolitan Police, has been acquitted of charges dating back to 1986. During the trial, Virdi claimed the charges were a retaliatory campaign by the police following his involvement in a racism inquiry.

Newly re-appointed Welsh minister Mr. Cairns argued that the UK should not remain in the EU single market, as both major political parties oppose membership. He also noted that the Welsh Government's calls for "unfetterer access" are essentially the same as the push for "frictionless trade." Meanwhile, several MPs are calling for a more flexible, cross-party consensus to ensure a stable Brexit deal that supports business.

Following the inquests that found the victims of the 1989 Hillsborough disaster were unlawfully killed, Home Secretary Theresa May held private meetings with grieving families to discuss ongoing criminal investigations. During these heated discussions, families expressed concerns regarding the conduct of South Yorkshire Police and advocated for the implementation of a new "Hillsborough Law" to increase accountability for public officials. Meanwhile, the Independent Police Complaints Commission is preparing to submit files to the Crown Prosecution Service as part of a massive inquiry into alleged police misconduct during the original investigation.

New guidance from the Crown Prosecution Service clarifies that inciting online harassment and "virtual mobbing" can result in the same legal consequences as offline offenses. While emphasizing that these rules are not intended to stifle free speech, the guidance aims to help police more easily identify crimes like doxxing and gross abuse.

Faizan, a young student, was killed by paramilitary gunfire during a violent protest occurring near a polling station in Kashmir. He was one of eight people killed during the chaos, which saw a historically low voter turnout as locals boycoted the election.

A woman has died following a collision involving a silver Ford Transit truck on Friday afternoon in Talysarn, Gwynedd. She was airlifted to Ysbyty Gwynedd before passing away, and North Wales Police are now appealing for witnesses to come forward.

Four companies submitted bids for the next Wales and Borders rail franchise, which will focus on a "not for profit" model to facilitate major network upgrades and the Metro scheme. The successful bidder will operate under a profit cap, with surplus funds being reinvested into Welsh public transport. A decision on the contract is expected to be announced in early 2后的 20.

After more than three decades, legendary broadcaster Robbie is stepping down from his long-running BBC Scotland show, *Take the Floor*. The 80-year-old veteran, known for his passion for traditional Scottish music, will pass the hosting duties to a younger presenter following his final program this weekend.

Following floods at Brunton Park, Carlisle United have scheduled several "home" matches at neutral grounds, including a victory against Notts County at Preston. Stanley manager Coleman expressed frustration with the league's decision, arguing that playing at neutral venues provides an unfair advantage to Carlisle.

Two supporters were discovered during a security sweep at Old Trafford after getting separated from their group during a stadium tour. While the pair was handed over to police, no arrests were made, and United confirmed there was no risk to fans attending upcoming matches.

Accrington Stanley defeated higher-league opposition Preston North End 3-2 in an EFL Cup derby after multiple lead changes in the match. Following a back-and-forth battle, Billy Kee secured the victory with a decisive stoppage-time header.

After a viral Facebook post regarding the accidental disappearance of his tools, 39-year-old Andrew Bickel has experienced a brief moment of national fame. He plans to donate any money earned from his story to both cat and dog charities to ensure no one is left out of pocket.

Middle-distance runner Muir has announced she will miss next year's Commonwealth Games due to conflicting schedules with her veterinary medicine studies. Despite being "gutted" about missing the event, she remains optimistic about her athletic future and is currently targeting the World Indoor Championships in March.

Former Newcastle striker Nile Ranger was sentenced to eight months in prison for online banking fraud, leading to uncertainty regarding his future with Southend. Manager Phil Brown expressed that the player needs a period of training to regain match fitness before the season begins on August 5.

Veteran broadcaster Sir Terry Wogan has died at the age of 77 following a brave battle with cancer. Tributes from colleagues and public figures, including Prime Minister David Cameron, have poured in to honor his legendary 50-year career and his ability to bring joy to millions of listeners.

Unions at BAE Systems have warned that delays to the production schedule for new Royal Navy frigates could lead to the loss of up to 800 jobs. While political leaders debate the impact on Scottish shipyards, the Scottish Conservatives maintain that the government's original orders and timetable remain unchanged. BAE Systems stated they are working with the Ministry of Defence to finalize a revised production schedule and baseline for the vessels.

During a heated Republican debate, Senators Marco Rubio and Ted Cruz launched aggressive attacks on Donald Trump’s business record and conservative credentials. Despite the personal insults and shifting focus toward the front-runner, Trump remained largely unbowed as the candidates prepared for the upcoming Super Tuesday contests.

Ukraine's Jamala won the Eurovision Song Contest, defeating favorites Russia and Australia with a historic victory for the first Crimean Tatar performer. While her song "1944" addressed historical themes of ethnic cleansing and Soviet deportation, the win sparked debate among experts regarding whether the contest had become a political platform.

Rother District Council has allocated £51,000 to fund lifeguard patrols at Camber Sands following a series of tragic drowning incidents involving seven men. The decision aims to enhance visitor safety and protect the local tourism economy after several unprecedented deaths occurred over the summer. The council intends to work with other agencies to ensure visitors are better informed about sea dangers while awaiting official inquest results.

Partick Thistle players expressed their desire to keep manager Tony Archibald following links to other vacancies after his successful top-six finish last season. While the team is also facing the potential loss of defender Liam Lindsay to Barnsley, players emphasized how much they value Archibald's leadership and stability.

Ten individuals were detained at Montreal's Trudeau International Airport after their passports were confiscated, pending ongoing investigations. While no charges have been filed, the arrests were made as part of efforts to protect communities from global terror threats.

After making a debut for the Tigers in August, 21-year-old former under-21 captain Dixon is set to move to the bottom-placed Minstermen. He is expected to make his debut for the club this Saturday against Newport.

The government has proposed new measures to curb "health tourism" and recover costs after a report estimated that foreign-related expenses cost the NHS £2bn annually. Proposed solutions include a levy on non-European temporary residents and improved recovery of funds from reciprocal-agreement nations, aiming to save £500m to fund 4,000 additional doctors. While critics and medical professionals have raised concerns regarding the accuracy of the data and the administrative burden on GPs, Health Secretary Jeremy Hunt maintains that these changes will ensure the NHS remains a national service rather than an international one.

The Belfast Giants secured a dominant 5-1 victory over the Devils, with goals from Colin Shields, Ryan Martinelli, Mark Garside, Alex Foster, and Steve Saviano. The win keeps the Giants in control of their busy festive schedule as they prepare for upcoming matchups against Manchester Storm and Coventry Blaze.

After undergoing significant restoration, a historic steam engine will make its first journey in ten years along the East Coast mainline. Originally built in Doncaster, the locomotive became an icon of British engineering after touring the world following its retirement from service in 1ً.

Only one out of five initial claimants has successfully been awarded compensation in a High Court case involving historical sexual abuse at St William's residential school. The ruling follows the imprisonment of former head James Carragher and former chaplain Anthony McCallen for their historical offences at the school. Further compensation claims from the 249 men involved are expected to be heard in late 2017.
